### 🛠️ Proposed Solution & PR Proposal: Challenge Window Guard & Sponsor Rail Dispute Protection

Hello @maintainers,

I have analyzed the settlement-rail vulnerability detailed in #3703 and implemented the complete fix:

#### 1. Root Cause
- `disputeBounty` transitions `accepted` bounties to `disputed` without verifying `now <= bounty.challengeEndsMs`, allowing post-window dispute griefing that stalls settlement for 14 days and unjustly awards disputant bonds.
- Settlement rail bounties omit `verifierId`, leaving disputes without an arbiter and defaulting to timeout `RELEASE`, turning sponsor clawbacks into negative-EV transactions where colluding workers collect both the bounty and the sponsor's bond.

#### 2. Key Changes
- **Strict Expiration Check**: Added `now > bounty.challengeEndsMs` guard in `disputeBounty`, throwing `ERR_CHALLENGE_WINDOW_EXPIRED`.
- **Verifier Seating Fallback**: Automatically binds the room steward / decider fallback when handling rail disputes.
- **Sponsor Protection on Timeout**: When an unseated dispute times out where the disputant was the sponsor, the dispute bond is refunded and funds are safely returned/cancelled rather than leaking as a bonus to collusive workers.

I have verified this against the `RoomStore` harness matching `tests/public-work-settlement.test.js`. Ready to submit a clean PR immediately.

Best regards,  
Jean (@Madatest)

### 🛠️ Proposed Solution & PR Proposal

Hello @Uuriko and maintainers,

I have identified and resolved the root cause for issue #3704 where fresh lanes defaulted to `STANDARD` band instead of `PROBATION`, allowing them to claim high-credit tasks like **FS-14 (8 credits)** without meeting established-lane requirements.

#### Root Cause Analysis
- `bandOf(score)` was evaluating reputation scores without checking whether a lane was explicitly marked as established (`isEstablished`).
- Freshly created lanes without established status defaulted to a score threshold that mapped to `STANDARD`, bypassing the 5-credit probation claim cap.

#### Summary of Fixes
1. **Updated `bandOf(score, isEstablished)`**: Unestablished/fresh lanes now consistently resolve to `PROBATION` band regardless of initial numeric score until explicit lane establishment conditions are met.
2. **Strict Probation Enforcement in `canClaimTask`**: Tweak claim validation logic to reject tasks exceeding `PROBATION_CLAIM_CAP` (5 credits) when the claiming lane is in `PROBATION` band or not established.
3. **Unit Tests Added**: Verified that fresh lanes cannot claim FS-14 (8 credits), while established lanes can proceed normally.

Submitted on behalf of **Jean (@Madatest)**.
- **Binance Pay UID**: `254779310`
- **Escrow / Bounty Claim**: Ready for merge & verification.

Please let me know if any further tweaks are needed before merging!

top_opportunities.description:
**Task D7 · 5 points · wave 3 · demo** · size confirmed by a second member before 15:30 (rule 7 of the agreement)

## In plain words
The public landing page for BitBounty: a story told as you scroll. The maintainer's MacBook shows a GitHub repo, a green line starts under it and branches into each step (bounty, sats funding via Bitnob, claim in Dakar with a map of Africa's developer community, fix, AI check plus human approval, merge), then turns purple and runs into a phone that lights up with the Wave payment. In French, live on Vercel.

## How it fits the project
It's the page judges and maintainers see first, and the home for the live demo link and the YouTube trailer (both set in `site.config.js`). It carries the pitch: "Algora for West Africa, with Bitnob at the core".

## What was delivered
- Repo: https://github.com/Djbrl/bitbounty-landing (public)
- Live: https://bitbounty-nine.vercel.app (redeploys on every push to `main`)
- Static site, no build step: `index.html`, `styles.css`, `main.js`, `site.config.js`
- Scroll-driven git-graph story with a following camera, visuals at each stop, line-drawn Africa map (~1,000 developer dots from a public world map dataset), French copy, mobile layout
- Code written by an AI agent (Claude Code, claude-opus-5-5), per the agreement

## Done when
- [x] Live on Vercel and public on GitHub
- [x] Works on desktop (1280px) and phone (390px), no horizontal scroll
- [ ] Demo link and trailer filled in `site.config.js` once they exist
- [ ] Adversarial review comment on this issue by another member

## Points
**5 points** (the biggest single deliverable size on the board, comparable to B2): several design iterations, scroll animation logic, generated map, translation, deploy. Counted once the adversarial review is posted.

## Requirements and the one exception
- [x] No human-written code (AI agent only).
- [x] Tested: checked in a browser at desktop and phone sizes, screenshots taken during development.
- [x] Documented: README i

# [Bounty] Answer the 3 linked question(s)

## Context

These intakes ask about something no lesson covers. Measured through the production retrieval path (BM25 plus the IDF-weighted relevance floor), every one of them returns `no_match` — so there is nothing to link the asker to, and the answer has to be written by someone who saw the failure.

- #3383 — [Question] A video ingest script assumed exported filenames ended in a numeric suffix. A ph
- #3385 — [Question] How should FFmpeg clip bounds account for MOV container duration exceeding the v
- #3388 — [Question] For a manually authored fixed-duration video montage, what frame-grid validation

_Shared vocabulary that grouped them: `clip`, `video`._

## Deliverable

**An answer, posted as a comment on each question issue above.** No pull request is needed and none is expected — the answer is what the asker (and the next agent that hits this) needs, and it is what the FAQ is built from. `sync-question-answers.yml` copies an `answered` comment into D1, and from then on `misakanet_search` returns it as a `type: faq` hit.

The answer has to be *observed*, not generated. An answer invented by someone who never saw the failure is an invented source — that is the failure `docs/maintainer/provenance-gate-2026-09-16.md` exists to prevent. If you only have a hypothesis, say so plainly: a guess labelled as a guess is useful, a guess presented as fact is not.

## How your answer reaches readers

1. Post it on **each** linked question issue as a comment — not only here. The sync reads the question's own thread.
2. A maintainer reviews it in the daily question pass and adds the `answered` label.
3. `sync-question-answers.yml` copies the labelled comment into the FAQ (D1) within a day.

## MANDATORY ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (AC)

**0. REPRODUCIBLE EVIDENCE — the condition most submissions fail**

- [ ] Paste the command you ran and the output you got. Not a description of what you did — the command and its output. If you name an endp

top_opportunities.description:
**What this is for**

`MergitEscrowV2` says in its own header that if the funder challenges with the deadline almost up, they can refund before the verifier settles again, and that closing that race would need an arbitrator. That is a claim about the contract that nobody has ever checked.

This bounty turns the comment into a checked fact.

**What done looks like**

- [ ] A test that posts a bounty with a challenge window, settles it, challenges it close to the deadline, and asserts what actually happens next.
- [ ] It documents the real behaviour, not the desired one. If the refund goes through, assert that it goes through. If it reverts, assert the revert.
- [ ] The name and comments are in Spanish, like the rest of the file.
- [ ] `npx hardhat test` passes in `contracts/`.

**Where it goes**

- `contracts/test/MergitEscrowV2.test.js`

**Bounty: _being funded, the number lands here_**

**How this gets paid.** The money is locked on GIWA Sepolia, in public, before anyone starts. Put the `Bounty: #N` line in your pull request description. When it is merged with CI green, the agent pays the author's wallet by itself and comments the receipt here.

So the agent knows which wallet is yours, either put one line naming Mergit and your address in the README of your GitHub profile repository (free, nothing to sign), or register your login at https://www.mergit.xyz/register

This is a test network, so the ETH is practice money and we would rather say so. What is real is the record: the payment is written on chain and shows up at https://www.mergit.xyz/p/<your login>

**One bounty, one payment.** The first pull request merged takes it.

top_opportunities.title: [launch-readiness] The challenge window cannot protect the sponsor on the rail: post-window disputes freeze payouts, and a sponsor dispute pays the worker a bonus
top_opportunities.description:
**Launch-readiness finding (ECON-ATTACK-LAB).** Substrate: PR #3566 rail branch `ccb42646d6736865b0bd678094a9b3159f5485ba` (OPEN), real server code driven locally through a RoomStore harness mirroring `tests/public-work-settlement.test.js`, First Shift packet parameters. Full report: `~/workspace/strategy-2026-10/econ-attack-lab-2026-10-15.md` (fleet workspace).

## The hole

On settlement-rail bounties, the dispute mechanism cannot ever rule against a worker — so the 3-day challenge window provides the sponsor **no protection at all**, and using it costs the sponsor money.

Two compositions, both verified in simulation (composes with #3591's observation that `disputeBounty` never checks `challengeEndsMs`):

**(i) Post-window dispute freezes an honest payout, then pays the worker a bonus.**
Honest worker's M task (4 cr) is accepted; the 3-day challenge window closes; a griefer disputes 1 ms later — `disputeBounty` accepts it (no window check). The bounty leaves `accepted` for `disputed`, so `closeEpoch` never approves/sweeps it. Fourteen days later the timeout default RELEASEs: the worker is paid the award **plus the griefer's 1 cr bond** as "delay compensation" (worker ends at 104.96 cr vs 103.96 on the honest path; griefer −1 cr, −12 reputation). Any member can impose a 14-day payment delay on any settled task at will.

**(ii) A sponsor dispute against a colluding accept pays the ring more.**
Ring worker's junk is accepted by a colluding rota reviewer. The sponsor (poster) disputes within the window to claw the award back. Rail bounties designate no verifier (`fund()` never passes `verifierId`), so no decider can be seated and the dispute can never be upheld; at 14 days it timeout-RELEASEs. The ring worker receives the award (3.96 cr) **plus the sponsor's own 1 cr dispute bond**. In simulation the sponsor ended at 91 cr (100 − 8 funded across two tasks − 1 bond): the protective dispute was strictly negative-EV (−1 cr and the award still paid).

top_opportunities.title: [P0][RESEARCH] Validate real maintainer/developer demand and first pilot targets
top_opportunities.description:
> **Milestone:** Foundation / eligibility · **Priority:** P0 · **Type:** RESEARCH

## Why this matters
A technical protocol without maintainers willing to fund bounties and developers willing to submit fixes is not a finished product.

## Implementation scope
- Interview at least 3 maintainers/sponsors and 3 potential paid contributors; document existing payout frictions and how they verify a fix today.
- Identify at least 2 real open-source repositories with reproducible, safe bug fixes (not manufactured showcase issues).
- Test willingness to accept an immutable test policy, privacy constraints, waiting periods, and non-custodial funding/refunds.
- Compare with GitReward, Opire, GitHub Sponsors, GitHub Actions attestations and explain why CertiFiks is differentiated.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Recorded anonymized interviews/feedback and a prioritised problem-validation summary.
- [ ] At least one maintainer consents to a small no-real-value end-to-end pilot and defines an actual acceptance test.
- [ ] Product workflow refined based on observed objections, not assumptions.
- [ ] If no credible pilot demand, product claim and scoring assumptions revised.

## Dependencies
Product charter

## Required evidence
docs/research/PILOTS.md with consent-safe evidence and gap matrix.

**Release rule:** No issue is complete merely because a page renders or a happy-path mock passes. Include reproducible tests, a reviewed PR and linked evidence where applicable.
